annotations.title: Check a BeatScript program

tools.description:
Check a BeatScript program without playing it: parse, type-check and compile the text. ALWAYS call check before eval, share or render, and fix every error at its line:col before trying again: a program with an error is refused whole. Warnings do not block.

Answers {ok, errors, warnings, diagnostics[{severity, line, col, end_col, message, expected, found, help, render}], cid, canonical, tempo, key, sections, song_bars, seconds, evolve, uses_assets, restricted, docs}. docs is the text's doc comments, [{kind, name, doc}]: the `#` lines directly above a section, let, def or arrange (a comment, so the CID does not change); sections[].doc is a section's, when it has one. line and col are 1-based; help says what would fix it ("did you mean ..."); render is the same error in caret form. ok:false is an answer, not a tool error. cid and canonical are of the canonical text (comments and spacing do not change the CID).

With same_as (another program's CID or text) the answer gains same_as {same, text_same, basis, why, diffs[{section, deck, start_bar, a_cid, b_cid}], only_in_a, only_in_b, renamed, song, diff}: whether the two are the same song by their compiled nets and song-level settings, not their text. When they are not, diff says what changed in music: diff.summary is one line per change ("tempo 124 -> 126", "moved outro: bar 13 -> bar 5", "drop2 bass = drop bass transposed +1", "drop bass: 1 note changed (1:7 c3 -> d3)"), with song, arrangement (inserted, removed, moved, repeated, renamed, changed) and parts (a transform: transpose, octave, rotate, reverse, thin, fill, fast, slow; else the notes added, removed or changed at bar:step) as JSON. Use it to prove a refactor changed nothing, or to find what an edit did.

This is the loop for writing a program (there is no compose tool): read https://btw.bitwrap.io/docs/cheatsheet.md and one or two list_examples programs, call instruments, write the program, call check and fix every line:col error until ok, then eval / load to play it and share to store it. Voices come from the instruments tool: use only names from it. For a sung line, a public-domain phrasebook line (list_examples with phrasebook true) comes with its meter, stress and phoneme escapes, so that sing @id on melody checks with no unknown-word warning (https://btw.bitwrap.io/docs/found-phrases.md). A voice name with a leading digit (808-bass) cannot be written: inst=808-bass reads as 808 - bass and a quoted "808-bass" is refused, so pick a voice that starts with a letter (inst=sub-bass for a deep bass). Read-only, no sign-in. Limits: the text is at most 16384 bytes; about 60 calls a minute.

Lexicon harvest, a side effect with no flag: when the program checks and may be kept (no samples or loops, no `use restricted`, public visibility; push_private records nothing), the (word, phonemes) pairs of its lyrics are recorded to grow the CC0 lexicon: each annotated escape word=/phonemes/ (jingle=/j ii ng g uh l/ sings the escape and keeps the word) and each word no lexicon knows, with the rules' pronunciation. Only the word, its phonemes and the program's CID are kept, never the text. The answer's lexicon is {harvested, new}: the pairs taken from this program, and how many no program had given before. When check says a word is not in the lexicon and it sounds wrong, write it as word=/phonemes/.

genre.description: Optional: a genre of the bitwrap ontology (techno, house, jazz, ... or its https://ontology.bitwrap.io/genre/ IRI); else the program's own `#! genre:` line. The answer gains style {genre, label, warnings[{severity: "style", code, message, line?, col?}]}: advice from the genre's conventions in the ontology (a tempo outside its range, a kit or voice the genre and its family do not use, chords far from its progressions). Style warnings never make ok false.

same_as.description: Optional: another program to compare with, as its CID (stored here, or an example's), a short https://btw.bitwrap.io/p/<CID> link, or its text. The answer gains same_as: whether the two are the same song by their compiled nets and song-level settings (tempo, key, swing, length, end, loop), not their text: a let/def/repeat refactor or a renamed section is the same song; a changed note is not, and diff says what changed in music (song settings, sections moved or inserted, a part transposed or rotated, notes at bar:step).

text.description: The program text (at most 16384 bytes). Comments and blank lines are fine.

tools.name: check

annotations.title: Your paired phones

tools.description:
List the phones paired with the token's account (djrust on Android scans the QR code that https://btw.bitwrap.io shows under Mobile; btwsite/PAIRING.md): id, name, fingerprint (the code both ends showed at pairing), paired, connected (djrust has its stream open now), last_seen, and state (what it last reported: cid, playing, section, bar). Pairing is the grant: a phone paired by an account is driven over MCP with that account's token and no other.

Pass a phone's id as device to eval, load, get or stop to drive that phone alone (eval and load run the same checks as for a tab; a program with errors, samples or "use restricted" is not sent). Needs a bearer token. Read-only.

annotations.title: Play a program in a browser tab

tools.description:
Send a program to a browser tab that has https://btw.bitwrap.io open, as if the user pressed Cmd+Enter in the editor: the text replaces the editor's and the change lands on the next bar, with no gap; play:true starts playback too. Needs a bearer token.

A tab must be connected. It is the page's own connection, so ask the user to open https://btw.bitwrap.io in a browser (signed in as the same account as the token, and eval reaches every live tab of that account), or, for a tab that is not signed in, to press MCP in the page's top bar and give you the session id it shows, which you pass as session. With no tab connected the answer is a no_session error that says this.

Run check first. eval checks too and refuses a program with errors (nothing is sent; the diagnostics come back), and one that uses samples or "use restricted" (the browser has no such files). The program is the user's to hear: do not eval over something they are playing without saying so. After eval call get to see what is playing, the section and bar, and any diagnostics the page itself reports. The text is formatted on the way in, as fmt does (header lines and comments kept), so the editor shows it tidy. Text is at most 16384 bytes.

Lexicon harvest, a side effect with no flag: when the program checks and may be kept (no samples or loops, no `use restricted`, public visibility; push_private records nothing), the (word, phonemes) pairs of its lyrics are recorded to grow the CC0 lexicon: each annotated escape word=/phonemes/ (jingle=/j ii ng g uh l/ sings the escape and keeps the word) and each word no lexicon knows, with the rules' pronunciation. Only the word, its phonemes and the program's CID are kept, never the text. The answer's lexicon is {harvested, new}: the pairs taken from this program, and how many no program had given before. When check says a word is not in the lexicon and it sounds wrong, write it as word=/phonemes/.

device.description: Id of one of your paired phones (djrust on Android), from the devices tool. Targets that phone alone; do not combine with session.

play.description: Start playing too (default false: load it and leave it stopped, or leave a playing tab as it is).

session.description: Session id of one browser tab, from the MCP panel of the page. Leave out to use your own signed-in tabs (every live one for eval/load/stop, the latest for get).

text.description: The program text. It must pass check.

tools.name: eval

annotations.title: Write out a program's seeds and templates

tools.description: Write out every seed(...) and template(...) of a BeatScript program as the plain BeatScript it stands for, to start from a generated track and edit it. seed(genre, n[, structure]) is a track of the beats generator (genres: ambient blues bossa country dnb dubstep edm funk garage house jazz lofi metal reggae speedcore synthwave techno trance trap; structures: standard, loop, minimal, extended), and it is a value, never audio: `arrange from seed(techno, 42)` is the whole track, `section intro from seed(techno, 42)[1..8]` its first eight bars as a section, and `bass seed(techno, 42).bass[17..24]` (or `let riff = seed(techno, 42).bass[17..24]`) one part's bars as a pattern. template(name, phrase) compiles a phrase, a phrasebook id (@tempest_such_stuff) or any words in quotes, to a whole track, `arrange from template(deep-house, @tempest_such_stuff)` (templates: deep-house): the phrase is the vocal line, its syllables the line's length, its stress the accents and the beats, its meter the subdivision, and the arrangement is the template's own. check, eval and share take the references as they are and play the same music (the CID is of the short text); expand gives the long text, with a `# from seed(...)` or `# from template(...)` line over each place it wrote, to edit from there. Answers {ok, text, canonical, cid, from_cid, refs, diagnostics}: cid is the written-out program's, from_cid the one you gave; with lineage true the text opens with `#! forked-from: <from_cid>`. Read-only, no sign-in.

lineage.description: Open the written-out text with `#! forked-from: <CID of the program as given>` (default false), so that once it is shared it says what it came from.

text.description: The program text, with seed(...) or template(...) references in it.

tools.name: expand

annotations.title: Format a BeatScript program

tools.description: Format a BeatScript program as the editor's fmt button does: one statement a line, one space between tokens, blocks indented two spaces, numbers, notes and chords spelled one way; the `#!` header lines, the comments and the blank lines between blocks stay where they are. Answers text (the formatted program), canonical (the same with no comments or header lines: the CID is of that), cid and comments. Formatting never changes the CID, so use fmt to tidy a program or to compare two; eval, load, queue, share and push_private already format what they are given. A program that does not parse answers the same diagnostics as check. Read-only, no sign-in.
tools.name: fmt

annotations.title: Generate a track from a seed (no model)

tools.description:
Generate a whole BeatScript track from a seed, with no model and no sign-in: the beats generator picks the genre's rhythms (Euclidean), chord progression, instruments and song structure from the seed, and the result is printed as readable source (named lets, a def for the shared groove, sections, an arrange, filter ramps, the chords as Roman numerals and e()/arp()/markov()/every/rotate/degrade with their seeds written out, so one `key` line moves the whole song) for you to edit. Same genre, bpm, key, length and seed: the same text and CID, every time; the seed and generator are in the #! header so the track can be re-derived. The program passes check and is stored as public CC0 (source generate). Answers text, cid, name, seed, generator, url and render_url; play it with eval or load, or edit it and check again.

Lexicon harvest, a side effect with no flag: when the program checks and may be kept (no samples or loops, no `use restricted`, public visibility; push_private records nothing), the (word, phonemes) pairs of its lyrics are recorded to grow the CC0 lexicon: each annotated escape word=/phonemes/ (jingle=/j ii ng g uh l/ sings the escape and keeps the word) and each word no lexicon knows, with the rules' pronunciation. Only the word, its phonemes and the program's CID are kept, never the text. The answer's lexicon is {harvested, new}: the pairs taken from this program, and how many no program had given before. When check says a word is not in the lexicon and it sounds wrong, write it as word=/phonemes/.

genre.description: The genre whose rhythms, chords, instruments and song structure it uses (default techno).

key.description: Key: am, c, f#m, d:dorian ...; default the genre's.

seed.description: A number or a word (default 1). Same inputs, same program text and CID.

tools.name: generate

annotations.title: A starting program for a genre

tools.description:
A starting BeatScript program for a genre, built from the bitwrap ontology's data for it (https://ontology.bitwrap.io, CC0): its tempo, key (root and scale), swing, drum kit and Euclidean kick, snare and hihat rhythms, its bass, arp and melody voices, its first chord progression (the chords, bass, arp and melody are Roman numerals, so a `key` line moves them all), and its family's standard song structure, each section with the roles the family's section profile makes active and its usual length. Returns {text, cid, canonical, seconds, genre{genre, label, family, tempo, tempo_range, scale, kit, voices, progressions, sections}} (and phrase, warnings with a phrase). The text passes check (it is checked before it is returned) and carries a `#! genre:` line, so check reports its style against the genre. Edit it, check it, then play or share it. For vocals, pass phrase (a phrasebook id from list_examples with phrasebook true, or any words): it is sung on the melody part of each section that has one, and the answer gains phrase with its source, year, meter, stress, syllables and phoneme escapes and whether its meter fits the genre (https://beatscript.app/docs/found-phrases.md). For a classical form, pass form (quodlibet, passacaglia, canon, rondo, fugue or theme-and-variations): the program is that form's template at the genre's tempo, built from public-domain themes, with the phrase (or the form's own) sung in it, and the answer gains form (its sections, mutation plan, themes and reference track) and expanded (the program written out to edit). To borrow one theme instead, pass theme (an id from list_examples with themes true): its lets go in, moved to the genre's key, played by the part of its role. See https://beatscript.app/docs/forms.md. For a whole track made from a phrase, write `arrange from template(deep-house, "your words")` (see expand). Read-only, no sign-in.

Lexicon harvest, a side effect with no flag: when the program checks and may be kept (no samples or loops, no `use restricted`, public visibility; push_private records nothing), the (word, phonemes) pairs of its lyrics are recorded to grow the CC0 lexicon: each annotated escape word=/phonemes/ (jingle=/j ii ng g uh l/ sings the escape and keeps the word) and each word no lexicon knows, with the rules' pronunciation. Only the word, its phonemes and the program's CID are kept, never the text. The answer's lexicon is {harvested, new}: the pairs taken from this program, and how many no program had given before. When check says a word is not in the lexicon and it sounds wrong, write it as word=/phonemes/.

form.description: Optional (docs/btw/forms.md): a classical form, one of quodlibet, passacaglia, canon, rondo, fugue, theme-and-variations. The program is then that form's template at the genre's tempo, arrange from template(<form>, <phrase>), and the answer gains form (shape, mutation plan, themes, reference track) and expanded (the program written out as plain BeatScript). Not with theme.

genre.description: A genre of the bitwrap ontology: its name (techno, house, jazz, dnb, ...), genre:<name>, or its https://ontology.bitwrap.io/genre/ IRI.

phrase.description: Optional, for vocals (found phrases, see docs/btw/found-phrases.md): a phrasebook id (tyger_burning_bright, from list_examples with phrasebook true) or any words. It is sung on the melody part of each section that has one, and the answer gains phrase: its source, year, meter, stress, syllables and phoneme escapes, and whether its meter fits the genre.

theme.description: Optional (docs/btw/forms.md): a theme of the public-domain theme library (ode_to_joy, pachelbel_ground, from list_examples with themes true). Its lets go into the program, moved to the genre's key, and the part of its role plays it in every section that has one; the answer gains theme. Not with form.

tools.name: genre_template

annotations.title: What a browser tab is playing

tools.description:
What a browser tab at https://btw.bitwrap.io is doing now, as the page last reported it: the program text and cid, playing (true/false), source (engine or stream), section (name), section_num of sections_total, bar, bars_in_section, phase (0-7, the light in the phrase), marks (what is firing: active lines, token flashes, ramps and timed lines, with line:col spans into the text), diagnostics (the page's own check of the text), ts, mixer (what the listener hears: crossfader, master, and per deck its level, mute, EQ kills, filter, insert filter and vocoder; null from a page or phone too old to report it) and warnings (a playing deck that cannot be heard, and why: "deck B inaudible: the crossfader is all the way to A"). Use it after eval or load to confirm the change landed, and to see the program a user is playing and editing.

Needs a bearer token: it reads the tabs of the token's account, by default the most recently seen one. A tab that is not signed in is read by its session id (the page's MCP panel shows it), with your token. Read-only. No tab connected: a no_session error that says how to connect one.

device.description: Id of one of your paired phones (djrust on Android), from the devices tool. Targets that phone alone; do not combine with session.

session.description: Session id of one browser tab, from the MCP panel of the page. Leave out to use your own signed-in tabs (every live one for eval/load/stop, the latest for get).

tools.name: get

annotations.title: Voices, kits and palettes

tools.description: The sounds a program may name: voices (inst=NAME), families (a name that contains one plays that family's generic voice and check warns about it), drum kits (kit=NAME) and palettes. Use only names from this answer: an unknown inst= is a check error with the nearest names. Read-only, no sign-in, cached for five minutes.
tools.name: instruments

annotations.title: A program's family tree

tools.description: A stored program's family tree, from the rights each program keeps (forked_from): its ancestors (nearest first), its siblings (the parent's other forks) and every generation of its forks, each edge labelled with what changed in music from parent to fork (the same diff summary lines check's same_as gives: "tempo 124 -> 126", "drop2 bass = drop bass transposed +1"; sameSong true when the fork only rewrote the text). Returns the JSON-LD document https://btw.bitwrap.io/p/<CID>/tree.jsonld serves: program, forkCount, descendantCount, ancestors, siblings and forks as CIDs, programs (name, licence, tempo, key, credits, url, forkCount of each), derivations (from, to, sameSong, change, and a compare URL, https://btw.bitwrap.io/p/<A>/compare/<B>). Only public programs appear: a private one is never listed, and a chain that passes through one stops there (ancestorsCut). A person can browse the same tree at https://btw.bitwrap.io/p/<CID>/tree.

cid.description: The program: its CID, or a short https://btw.bitwrap.io/p/<CID> link. It must be stored here (or be an example) and public.

tools.name: lineage

annotations.title: The example programs

tools.description: The public example programs of https://btw.bitwrap.io, all CC0-1.0: name, title, description, cid, bpm, bars, license and the url of the raw .btw. Pass name to get that program's full text as well. Read two or three before writing a program of your own: after the cheat-sheet (https://btw.bitwrap.io/docs/cheatsheet.md) they are the best guide to the language, from a four-line beat (first-beat) to whole tracks with sections, defs, ramps and evolve. With phrasebook true (or a meter, or syllables) it also returns the public-domain phrasebook: lines first published before 1929, each with its text, source, year, meter, stress pattern, syllables and phoneme escapes, to sing by id (sing @tempest_such_stuff on melody); choose one for its meter, see https://btw.bitwrap.io/docs/found-phrases.md. With themes true (or a key, a role or a composer) it also returns the public-domain theme library: melodies, basses and figures composed and published before 1929, each as BeatScript bars in a stated key with the let lines and the part that play it, its work, composer, year and the themes it morphs well with; borrow one as found material or build a form from it, see https://btw.bitwrap.io/docs/forms.md. Read-only, no sign-in.

composer.description: Only the themes by this composer (any part of the name: beethoven). Implies themes.

key.description: Only the themes in this key, matched on its tonic: a key word (d, bm, db). Implies themes.

lexicon.description: Also return the lexicon harvest (default false): the words the checking tools collected from programs' lyrics, ranked for the CC0 lexicon, at most 50: those with an annotated escape (word=/phonemes/) first, then by how many programs gave them. Each is {word, programs, conflict, in_lexicon, variants[{phones, source (annotated or rule), count, first, last, cids}]}; conflict: two annotated pronunciations disagree. Read-only.

meter.description: Only the phrasebook lines of this meter: a family (iambic, trochaic, anapestic, dactylic, common-meter, sprung, nursery, parallelism, oratory, call-and-response) or a word of a meter's name (pentameter). Implies phrasebook.

name.description: Optional: also return this example's full text.

phrasebook.description: Also return the public-domain phrasebook: lines first published before 1929, each with its text, source, year, meter, stress pattern, syllables and phoneme escapes (default false).

role.description: Only the themes of this role: melody, bass, harmony or arp. Implies themes.

syllables.description: Only the phrasebook lines with this many syllables: a number (8) or a range (8-12). Implies phrasebook.

themes.description: Also return the public-domain theme library: melodies, basses and figures composed and published before 1929, each as BeatScript bars in a stated key (let-ready), with its role, meter, work, composer, year and pairings (default false).

tools.name: list_examples

annotations.title: Listen to a program (a summary, no audio)

tools.description:
Listen to a BeatScript program without audio: it is rendered offline through the same engine as render, and you get a small JSON summary to check your work by ear, as numbers. Per deck and per part (a role of a deck's line: drums, bass, ...): RMS and peak in dBFS and loudness in LUFS. `silent` lists every deck or part that has notes in the window but is not heard (under -60 LUFS), with `reason` when the mixer explains it (master_zero, mute, level_0, crossfader, filter_closed, eq_killed; voice_missing when the mixer lets a part through and its voice made nothing; no_sound otherwise) and `why` in words. `detected` gives the tempo and key heard against the declared ones (bpm_match same|half|double|two_thirds|three_halves|differs; key_match same|relative|differs|unsure|undeclared). `sections` gives each section's loudness, `bar_lufs` a loudness per bar, and master.clipped_samples counts samples over full scale. `warnings` is the short list to act on. Give exactly one of text, cid, example; optionally `section` (listen to that section only) and `bars` (at most this many bars of the window). Nothing is stored and no sign-in is needed. At most 30 new listens an hour per caller; the same program, section and bars again is answered from the cache. Programs are at most 16384 bytes; the render covers at most 96 bars from the start. Like render, the offline engine plays the notes and the mixer and insert moves it has ops for; `notes` names the control lines it leaves out.

Lexicon harvest, a side effect with no flag: when the program checks and may be kept (no samples or loops, no `use restricted`, public visibility; push_private records nothing), the (word, phonemes) pairs of its lyrics are recorded to grow the CC0 lexicon: each annotated escape word=/phonemes/ (jingle=/j ii ng g uh l/ sings the escape and keeps the word) and each word no lexicon knows, with the rules' pronunciation. Only the word, its phonemes and the program's CID are kept, never the text. The answer's lexicon is {harvested, new}: the pairs taken from this program, and how many no program had given before. When check says a word is not in the lexicon and it sounds wrong, write it as word=/phonemes/.

bars.description: At most this many bars of the window, from its start.

cid.description: CID of a stored program or an example.

example.description: Name of an example, from list_examples.

section.description: Listen to this section only (its name in the program).

text.description: The program text. It must pass check. Not stored.

tools.name: listen

Only the word, its phonemes and the program's CID are kept, never the text. The answer's lexicon is {harvested, new}: the pairs taken from this program, and how many no program had given before. annotations.title: Open a share link

tools.description: Decode a BeatScript share link and return its canonical text, its CID and whether the CID verifies against the text. Takes either form: a self-sealing link (https://btw.bitwrap.io/#<CID>.<packed>, a /c/<CID>.<packed> link, a beats.bitwrap.io/p# link, a bare #fragment or <CID>.<packed>) or a CID-only link (https://btw.bitwrap.io/p/<CID>, /c/<CID>, https://beats.bitwrap.io/p/<CID>, #<CID>, or a bare CID), which is resolved from the programs the site has stored (shared signed in, or rendered) and the examples, and answers its rights in meta. Either way the text is recompiled and its CID recomputed: a program whose CID is not its text's is refused with cid_mismatch, and an unknown CID answers not_found. Do not trust or play a refused text. Comments carried in a link (notes) are unverified. Read-only, no sign-in.

url.description: A share link (self-sealing #<CID>.<packed>, or a short <site>/p/<CID> or /c/<CID> link), a #fragment, <CID>.<packed>, or a bare CID.

tools.name: open

annotations.title: Send a private program to your phone

tools.description: Send a private program to one of your paired phones, end-to-end encrypted, and never stored. Use it for what https://btw.bitwrap.io does not keep: covers, programs with local samples (`sample ... from`), `use restricted`, anything not under a Creative Commons licence. The program is sealed for the phone's own key (X25519 from its pairing key, ChaCha20-Poly1305) and handed to the phone's live connection in memory: it is not written to disk, a database or a log (only its size and the device id are logged), no CID is registered, and if the phone is not connected nothing is sent and nothing is kept (push again when it is). The phone opens it, checks it and plays it itself; samples resolve against files in the phone's own sample library, and any that are missing are reported back in get's diagnostics, never fetched. Give device and exactly one of text (sealed here, so the text is in this server's memory for this call, where it is formatted first, as eval's is) or sealed (an envelope you sealed yourself for the phone's seal_key from devices: then this server only ever sees ciphertext). Needs a bearer token; only your own paired phones.

device.description: Id of one of your paired phones, from the devices tool.

load.description: Load it on the phone and leave it stopped unless play (default false: play it as eval does).

play.description: Start playing too (default false: load it and leave it stopped, or leave a playing tab as it is).

sealed.description: An envelope you sealed for the phone's seal_key (btwseal v1). Give text or sealed.

text.description: The program text, sealed here for the phone. Give text or sealed.

tools.name: push_private

annotations.title: Up next: queue programs on a browser tab

tools.description:
An "up next" queue on one browser tab at https://btw.bitwrap.io (the same tabs and rules as load: session, or device, else your most recently seen signed-in tab). When the playing program ends the page plays the next item, on the bar line where it can; a looping program (one that never ends) plays for the item's bars or minutes, else one full pass of its arrangement, and then advances. Needs a bearer token.

action is one of: list (the queue, now_playing, position, paused_reason, listener), add (items: up to 20 per call, 50 in the queue), remove (item: an item id from list, or a CID), clear, skip (play the next item now).

Items must already be programs: {cid} of a stored program (render and a signed-in share store theirs) or an example's CID, {example} by name from list_examples, or {url} a share link (verified exactly as load verifies it; a CID-only link must name a stored program). Optional per item: bars (1-1024) or minutes (0.1-120) to play, title. THE QUEUE NEVER COMPOSES OR CALLS A MODEL, and there is no way to make it: to queue new music, write the programs yourself (check them), store each with render or share, then add the CIDs.

The queue advances only while a listener is plausibly present, as the page reports it: it pauses at the next track boundary when the tab's audio is suspended, when the tab has been hidden with no key, pointer, touch or media key for 30 minutes, or after 8 tracks in a row without any interaction; the page then shows "Still listening? Press play to continue". Only a person on the page lifts a pause: skip is refused while paused (paused_reason says why), and load still plays one program as it always has but does not resume the queue. Writes are limited to about 30 a minute. The queue lives with the tab's session and is gone when the tab is.

Lexicon harvest, a side effect with no flag: when the program checks and may be kept (no samples or loops, no `use restricted`, public visibility; push_private records nothing), the (word, phonemes) pairs of its lyrics are recorded to grow the CC0 lexicon: each annotated escape word=/phonemes/ (jingle=/j ii ng g uh l/ sings the escape and keeps the word) and each word no lexicon knows, with the rules' pronunciation. Only the word, its phonemes and the program's CID are kept, never the text. The answer's lexicon is {harvested, new}: the pairs taken from this program, and how many no program had given before. When check says a word is not in the lexicon and it sounds wrong, write it as word=/phonemes/.

action.description: list, add, remove, clear or skip.

device.description: Id of one of your paired phones (djrust on Android), from the devices tool. Targets that phone alone; do not combine with session.

item.description: remove: an item id from list (q1, q2, ...) or a CID (the first queued item with it).

items.description: add: the programs to append, each an object with exactly one of cid, example, url, and optionally bars, minutes, title.

bars.description: Play this many bars, then advance (else until the program ends; a loop: one arrangement pass).

cid.description: CID of a stored program or an example.

example.description: Name of an example, from list_examples.

minutes.description: Play this long, then advance at the next bar line. Not with bars.

title.description: What the page shows for it (else the program's name).

url.description: A share link, verified as load verifies it.

session.description: Session id of one browser tab, from the MCP panel of the page. Leave out to use your own signed-in tabs (every live one for eval/load/stop, the latest for get).

tools.name: queue

annotations.title: Set up a demo recording

tools.description: Set up a demo recording of a program: the page in record mode (full screen code, the firing markers and follow-scroll on) and the steps that turn it into a video. Give exactly one of text, cid or example (as render does: a text or example is checked and stored publicly as CC0-1.0, nothing private). Answers {cid, seconds, record_url, record_url_manual_clock, audio_url, recipe}. record_url opens the page in record mode and plays it for a person to screen-record; record_url_manual_clock opens it on a fake clock that a script steps frame by frame (window.__btw.setTime(seconds); window.__btw.frame()), which is how btwsite/tools/record-demo.mjs in the repo makes a perfectly synced, stutter-free MP4 (H.264, AAC, 1920x1080) plus a silent hero loop (MP4 and WebM) and a poster PNG, taking the audio from audio_url (the offline render of the same program). This tool does not capture video itself: it needs a browser and ffmpeg on your side. The audio is the offline render: notes and sounds, not control lines (filters, reverb). Call check first. Rendering limits apply (about 30 programs an hour per client). No sign-in needed.

cid.description: CID of a program already stored (for instance the cid render or a signed-in share returned).

example.description: Name of an example, from list_examples.

text.description: The program text. It must pass check; it is stored publicly (CC0-1.0).

tools.name: record

annotations.title: Render a program to streaming audio

tools.description:
Make a program streamable as audio. Give exactly one of text (the program), cid (a program already stored, e.g. what an earlier render or a signed-in share returned) or example (a name from list_examples). A text or example is checked, then stored publicly under its CID as CC0-1.0 if it is not stored yet (never submit anything private; programs that use samples or "use restricted" are refused). Answers {cid, stream_url, status_url, seconds, format}: open stream_url to listen (it streams the offline render as it renders; the first sound comes within about a second, so a client can play it at once), download the same URL for a file, and read status_url to see how far a render is. format is opus (Ogg Opus, small) or wav (16-bit stereo, plays chunk by chunk in a web page); default opus. To take the program to a DAW: format midi (a Standard MIDI File: a track per part, drums on channel 10 with General MIDI notes, the tempo map, key and section markers) or stems (a zip of a 32-bit float WAV per part and per deck that add up to the master, plus the master, the .mid and manifest.json with the CID, tempo, key and the stored license and credits; stems-opus: the same with Ogg Opus stems); a stems URL answers 202 while it is being made, ask again until it is the zip.

Call check first. The offline render plays the notes and sounds, not control lines (filters, reverb, do ... lines), so it can sound plainer than the browser; a program with no end (no sections or end line) is cut at the server's bar limit (256 bars). Rendering is limited per address per hour and to a few at once: on busy or rate_limited wait retry_after seconds. No sign-in needed; about 30 programs an hour per client.

Lexicon harvest, a side effect with no flag: when the program checks and may be kept (no samples or loops, no `use restricted`, public visibility; push_private records nothing), the (word, phonemes) pairs of its lyrics are recorded to grow the CC0 lexicon: each annotated escape word=/phonemes/ (jingle=/j ii ng g uh l/ sings the escape and keeps the word) and each word no lexicon knows, with the rules' pronunciation. Only the word, its phonemes and the program's CID are kept, never the text. The answer's lexicon is {harvested, new}: the pairs taken from this program, and how many no program had given before. When check says a word is not in the lexicon and it sounds wrong, write it as word=/phonemes/.

cid.description: CID of a program already stored (for instance the cid render or a signed-in share returned).

example.description: Name of an example, from list_examples.

format.description: opus (Ogg Opus, smaller, for download or <audio>) or wav (16-bit stereo, plays chunk by chunk in a web page) to listen; for a DAW: midi (a Standard MIDI File of the notes, a track per part), stems (a zip: a 32-bit float WAV per part and per deck that add up to the master, the master, the .mid and manifest.json with the CID, tempo, key, license and credits) or stems-opus (the same zip with Ogg Opus stems).

text.description: The program text. It must pass check; it is stored publicly (CC0-1.0).

annotations.title: Make share links

tools.description:
Make the share links of a program. Always the self-sealing link: https://btw.bitwrap.io/#<CID>.<base64url(deflate(canonical text))>; the program travels inside the link, and whoever opens it gets exactly that text, verified against the CID, and can play and fork it. Also social_url (https://btw.bitwrap.io/c/<CID>.<packed>, the form to post where a link preview is wanted: it carries a card image) and the same link on beats.bitwrap.io. Called signed in (a bearer token), it also stores the program on the site (public, with its rights: license, forked_from, credits, name; the first share's rights stay) and returns the CID-only forms: short_url (https://btw.bitwrap.io/p/<CID>), short_social_url (https://btw.bitwrap.io/c/<CID>) and short_beats_url (https://beats.bitwrap.io/p/<CID>), plus fetch_url, a public GET that returns the canonical text and rights for a phone or an app. Opening a short link fetches the text, recompiles it, recomputes the CID and refuses a mismatch. Anonymous calls get the self-sealing links and short_url null. The program must pass check and must not use samples or "use restricted" (a private program is never shared or stored); programs shared here are CC0 unless license says otherwise. The text is formatted on the way in (the stored and linked program is its canonical text, whose CID the header lines and comments do not change; a `#! name:` line names the stored program). Links over about 2000 characters (chars says) may be cut by some apps; short links are not. A stored program also embeds in other sites: embed_url (https://btw.bitwrap.io/embed/<CID>) is a player any page may frame, https://btw.bitwrap.io/embed.js gives <beatscript-player cid="<CID>">, and https://btw.bitwrap.io/oembed?url=<a /p/ or /c/ link> answers oEmbed; see https://btw.bitwrap.io/docs/embed. Who authored a program and what rights it has, in plain language: https://btw.bitwrap.io/authorship.

Lexicon harvest, a side effect with no flag: when the program checks and may be kept (no samples or loops, no `use restricted`, public visibility; push_private records nothing), the (word, phonemes) pairs of its lyrics are recorded to grow the CC0 lexicon: each annotated escape word=/phonemes/ (jingle=/j ii ng g uh l/ sings the escape and keeps the word) and each word no lexicon knows, with the rules' pronunciation. Only the word, its phonemes and the program's CID are kept, never the text. The answer's lexicon is {harvested, new}: the pairs taken from this program, and how many no program had given before. When check says a word is not in the lexicon and it sounds wrong, write it as word=/phonemes/.

credits.description: Who is credited, one short line each. Stored with the rights.

forked_from.description: CID of the program this one was forked from. Stored with the rights.

license.description: Rights kept with the stored program: a Creative Commons SPDX id (default CC0-1.0; CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0 and the like). The site stores no other licence: keep such a program local, or send it to your phone with push_private.

name.description: A name for the program (else its `#! name:` line).

text.description: The program text. It must pass check.

tools.name: share

annotations.title: Stop a browser tab

tools.description: Stop what a browser tab at https://btw.bitwrap.io is playing: the program ends and whatever its lines held (a filter, a mute) is put back. Reaches every live tab of the token's account, or one tab by session (the id the page's MCP panel shows). Needs a bearer token. No tab connected: a no_session error that says how to connect one.

device.description: Id of one of your paired phones (djrust on Android), from the devices tool. Targets that phone alone; do not combine with session.

session.description: Session id of one browser tab, from the MCP panel of the page. Leave out to use your own signed-in tabs (every live one for eval/load/stop, the latest for get).
